purpose: Fixtures the C backend cannot compile today. `emit_c` covers tests/c_emit (checked by c-test); `sweep` covers the tests/spec corpus as the emit sweep chunks it (checked by spec-emit-sweep.py). Each entry is still asserted: it must fail, and fail for the recorded reason. A fixture that starts passing, stops failing for its recorded reason, or begins failing without an entry here fails its gate. `E_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED` is the backend's single refusal code, so the code alone cannot tell one gap from another; every entry carrying it must also record a `cause` -- the refusing phase, category, construct and function the diagnostic names -- and the gates compare that, so a fixture that drifts to a different gap fails instead of resting on the entry written for the old one. The shape lives in tools/toolchain/backend_gap_lib.py.

sweep.note: The C emitter declines the fixture's kept chunk: C backend does not yet support a body left incomplete by `unsupported_cast` in `possibly_racing_raw_many_offset_zero_pointer_load` (declined by mir-build). This fixture is not one gap. Deleting each failing function and re-emitting enumerates 70 of them: 36 are a `range_slice` that constructs a slice whose elements are pointers -- the body renderer spells a slice type inline as `mc_slice_<mutability>_<child>`, which is a C identifier only for a primitive element, while a pointer element names a mangled typedef only the declaration collector frames; 15 are an aggregate pointer alias whose executable shape is incoherent; 5 an indirect call through a pointer alias copied from a parameter (declined as expression `local`); 5 an incoherent executable shape; 4 a trapping store of a pointer into an aggregate field; 3 a `*T as [*]T` cast kind neither `ExecutableCastKind.classify` nor either renderer has; 2 an array-element assignment. Closed on the way past: the `index` read over a slice of pointers. It was 36 of these, and they are the same 36 functions, now refused one step earlier at the range slice that builds the slice rather than at the read. See todo.md.
